quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Break "kick" down sound by sound. The consonant you want is either a voiceless velar plosive or a voiced velar plosive — remember that /k/ means you raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.
quests.explanation: The word "kick" contains /k/, a voiceless velar plosive, made by raising the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice. It's easy to confuse with /g/, a voiced velar plosive, but the two are produced quite differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "cot" at normal speed, then again in slow motion. Isolating the consonant this way makes it much easier to tell /k/ from /g/.
quests.explanation: "cot" is a good example of /k/: you raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice. Compare that with /g/, where you'd instead raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on — the two shouldn't be mixed up once you feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Listen closely to "dug". For /d/, you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on — like the start of "day". Does that match what you hear?
quests.explanation: The consonant in "dug" is /d/, not /t/. To produce /d/, you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on; /t/ is made differently, by tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel it in the mouth: tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: "cup" contains one of these two sounds. /k/ is a voiceless velar plosive, made when you raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice. /g/ is a voiced velar plosive instead.
quests.explanation: Here, /k/ is correct because "cup" is made by raising the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice. If it were /g/ instead, you'd be doing this: raising the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on — a noticeably different articulation.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "dab" slowly and isolate just the target consonant. To make /d/, you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on. To make /t/, you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice. Which one are you actually doing?
quests.explanation: "dab" uses /d/, a voiced alveolar plosive. This contrasts with the voiceless alveolar plosive /t/, heard in words like "tea", which is produced by tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice instead.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on.
